ITEM 2.  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Philip Falconbridge expressw concerns regarding Vice Chair Mazza's position on
  the Planning Commission and ongoing participation in Malibu Township Council
  appeals against Planning Commission decisions where the Commissioner
  dissented against the quorum’s approval. He stated the Vice Chair voted against
  California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) Pacific Coast Highway (PCH)
  safety measures based on his personal preference for darkness near his residence.
  He voiced concems regarding the actions of Malibu Township Council members
  Jo Drummond, Patt Healy, and Bill Sampson.

  Atticus noted Vice Chair Mazza‘s comment that the Caltrans PCH improvements
  project would be appealed at the prior meeting. which was caught on a live
  microphone, reflected the Commissioner‘s intent to orchestrate the Malibu
  Township Council appeal to push for street lighting reductions near his residence.
  He stated Vice Chair Mazza had made statements from the dais that were
  culturally inappropriate.

  Vice Chair Mazza expressed the belief that comments made by virtual speakers
  during public comment were based on the next year‘s election platform. He noted
  that the Malibu Township Council had a long history within the community and
  prevented potentially environmentally damaging projects. The Vice Chair stated
  that as a result of the appeal, additional safety improvements were agreed to by
  Caltrans and challenged the view that the appeal put $55 million in safety
  improvements at risk. He stated he was ashamed of both the Planning
  Commission and City Council's approval ofthe Caltrans PCH project.

  Commissioner Kamins expressed disappointment in virtual speakers who had
  made disparaging statements against volunteer Commissioners without being
  willing to appear in person.

  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR REPORT

  Associate Planner Azzaz presented a summary of rebuild statistics and
  highlighted upcoming meeting dates.
